note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world (how many courts a park has, whether it is lit, what a reservation costs) come from the City of Irvine and the City of Huntington Beach and are cited. Claims about coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Orange County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. This is the first county in California this directory has published in, and two cities of it are on this page.

slots.coverage:
Two cities in Orange County are published here, and both were read on the same day. Irvine has three venues and eighteen courts, every one of them lit in the City's own word: eight at Mike Ward Community Park, six at Portola Springs Community Park and four at Heritage Community Park. Huntington Beach has four venues and thirteen courts, every one of them unlit in the City's own word: four each at Edison Park, Marina Park and Worthy Park, and one at Boardwalk Park. That makes seven venues and thirty-one courts, eighteen of them lit and thirteen stated unlit, with no lighting silence anywhere.

Orange County contains many other cities, Anaheim, Santa Ana, Newport Beach and Costa Mesa among them, and none of those has been checked against a named source, so none appears anywhere on this site. One Irvine venue is absent by refusal rather than by omission. Los Olivos Community Park is credited with "two lit pickleball courts" on two City pages and "3 Lighted Pickleball Courts" on a third, and a count the operator states two ways cannot be published.
slots.distribution:
What is verified in this county splits cleanly on one fact, and the two cities sit on opposite sides of it. Irvine's eighteen courts are all lit and all in parks open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Huntington Beach's thirteen sit under a City heading that reads "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)", and the City states no hours for them at all. A player with a job has an evening in Irvine and does not have one in Huntington Beach.

The venues are of different kinds. Irvine's three are large community parks, approximately 22, 32 and 36.5 acres, with lit tennis, soccer, softball, basketball and racquetball beside the pickleball, community centres at two of them, and restrooms stated at all three. Huntington Beach's four get one line each on a Park Amenities page: name, address and count. One court at Boardwalk Park means one game at a time and no rotation.

Price divides the county the same way. Irvine prices two courts at each of its two largest venues, $17 an hour for residents and $19 for non-residents, and calls the rest first come, first served. Huntington Beach prices reserved tennis courts at $9 an hour and never prices or frees a pickleball court. Neither city writes the word free. Irvine also runs a league at Portola Springs and lessons at all three parks; Huntington Beach publishes nothing of that kind for pickleball.
slots.gaps:
The gap here is the size of the county. Two cities are read; Anaheim, Santa Ana, Newport Beach and Costa Mesa are not, and nothing on this page is an estimate of Orange County's pickleball. A city publishes when three or more of its venues carry a source and a date.

Irvine's gap is contradiction. The City's regulations page says it has "12 public pickleball courts"; its per-park sentence on the pickleball page adds to twenty, and its park pages add to twenty-one once the three at Los Olivos are counted. Its hybrid tennis-and-pickleball courts number ten on one page, nine on another and eight in a third sentence, and never have a per-park figure, so Knollcrest, San Carlo, Turtle Rock and University are not venues here despite being named by the City.

Huntington Beach's gap is silence. Hours, price, surface and indoor or outdoor are unstated for every pickleball court, and Worthy Park carries two City addresses, 1831 17th Street beside the count and 1801 Main Street on the tennis page. Clubs, HOAs and commercial venues may well hold courts in Orange County, and none of them publishes a source this site has read.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Orange County?
faqs.a: No honest page can tell you. What has been checked is 31 courts across seven venues in two cities, 18 in Irvine and 13 in Huntington Beach, each with a source and a date you can see. Every other city in the county is unread.

faqs.q: Why is Los Olivos Community Park not listed?
faqs.a: Because the City of Irvine states two counts for it: "two lit pickleball courts" on its pickleball page and its regulations page, and "3 Lighted Pickleball Courts" on the park's own page. This site publishes the number an operator states, and cannot publish when the operator states two.

sources.evidence: The City of Irvine's pickleball page. "The City of Irvine has eight lit pickleball courts located at Mike Ward Community Park, six lit pickleball courts located at Portola Springs Community Park, four lit pickleball courts located at Heritage Park, and two lit pickleball courts located at Los Olivos Community Park. In addition, there are 10 hybrid tennis and pickleball courts located at the following parks: Heritage, Knollcrest, Los Olivos, Portola Springs, San Carlo, Turtle Rock, and University." Reservations at Portola Springs (Courts #5 and #6) and Mike Ward (Courts #3 and #4): "Resident Rate: $17/hr", "Non-Resident Rate: $19/hr". Lessons at all three parks; the Irvine Team Pickleball league at Portola Springs Community Park. Snapshot: data/sources/irvine/pickleball.html
sources.not_stated: Anything about any other municipality in Orange County, the word free, and any per-park count for the hybrid courts.

sources.evidence: The City of Irvine's court regulations page. "Open courts are on a first-come, first-serve basis." "The City of Irvine has 96 public tennis courts, 12 public pickleball courts, and 8 public hybrid tennis/pickleball courts." "The City of Irvine has eight lit pickleball courts located at Mike Ward Park, six lit pickleball courts located at Portola Springs Community Park, and two lit pickleball courts at Los Olivos Community Park. In addition, there are nine hybrid tennis and pickleball courts". Snapshot: data/sources/irvine/court-regulations-and-map.html
sources.not_stated: Any count for Heritage Park, which its list omits, and any reconciliation of its 12 with the per-park counts.

sources.evidence: Heritage Community Park's page, the largest published park in the county: "Approximately 36.5 acres in size", "4 Lighted Pickleball Courts", "12 Lighted Tennis Courts", "4 Restrooms", "Heritage Park Community Center", "Hours: 6 a.m.-10 p.m., Daily", at "14301 Yale Ave. Irvine, CA 92604". Mike Ward's page gives "Approximately 22.0 acres", "3 Restrooms" and the same hours; Portola Springs's gives "Approximately 32 acres", "2 Restrooms", a community centre and the same hours. Snapshot: data/sources/irvine/heritage-community-park.html
sources.not_stated: Parking, surface, price, and a count for the hybrid courts the City places here.

sources.evidence: Los Olivos Community Park's page, the refused Irvine venue: "3 Lighted Pickleball Courts" in the amenity list, at "101 Alfonso Irvine, CA 92618". The City's pickleball page and regulations page both say "two lit pickleball courts" for the same park. Snapshot: data/sources/irvine/los-olivos-community-park.html
sources.not_stated: Any reconciliation of the three-court line with the two-court sentence.
